mainTopic: End of the Creation אגדה, the משנה on working on תשעה באב, and the גמרא on its twilight and washing rules
overview: This amud first finishes an אגדה section. It ends the list of things created on the first ערב שבת with the garment of אדם הראשון. Then come two ברייתות: seven things hidden from people, and things הקב"ה built into the world because it needs them. Next a new משנה says that working on תשעה באב follows local מנהג. תלמידי חכמים refrain everywhere, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says anyone may act like a תלמיד חכם. The גמרא then discusses whether eating during the בין השמשות of תשעה באב is forbidden. שמואל permits it. רבא, also in the name of רבי יוחנן, forbids it. The גמרא works through several readings of רבי יוחנן's words 'תשעה באב is not like a תענית ציבור': work, נעילה, the twenty-four ברכות, and רב פפא's stringency. A ברייתא comparing תשעה באב to יום הכיפורים is explained as referring to doubt about the date of ראש חודש, and this supports רבי אלעזר's ban on dipping even a finger in water. A final challenge from washing rules on a תענית ציבור is answered by רב פפא on the next amud.

steps.title: Last item: the garment of the first man
steps.stepSummary: The list of things created בין השמשות of the first ערב שבת closes with the garment of אדם הראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The garment of the first man (was also created then).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final item in a list from the previous lines. It names things הקב"ה created at twilight right before the first שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment is the 'garments of skin' הקב"ה made for אדם and חוה (בראשית ג:כא). By placing it in this list, the ברייתא teaches that even this garment was prepared at the very end of the six days of Creation.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a list that began on the previous amud (things created בין השמשות).

phrases.english: The garment of Adam, the first man.
phrases.notes: Refers to the 'garments of skin' of Genesis 3:21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of things created בין השמשות from the preceding (previous-passage) ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The garment of אדם הראשון was among the things created at twilight of the first ערב שבת.

steps.title: Seven things hidden from people
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists seven matters that human beings cannot know.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Seven things are hidden from people. They are: the day of death, the day of comfort, the depth of judgment, what is in another person's heart, how one will make a living, when the kingdom of דוד will return, and when the wicked kingdom will end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא listing seven things people cannot know. It continues the theme of special hidden matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item is something only הקב"ה controls. These include personal timing (death, relief from troubles), truth in judgment, other people's thoughts, and livelihood. The list ends with national redemption: the return of מלכות בית דוד and the fall of the wicked kingdom (Rome).

keyTerms.meaning: the day of consolation (relief from worry)
the depth of judgment (the true outcome of a case)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Seven things are hidden from people,
and they are: the day of death,
the day of consolation, and the depth of judgment,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ מָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: and a person does not know what is in his fellow's heart,
and a person does not know through what he will profit,
and when the kingdom of the House of David will return,
and when the wicked kingdom will come to an end.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים מְכוּסִּים מִבְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related אגדה list, brought because it follows a list of special things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven matters (death, consolation, true judgment, others' thoughts, livelihood, the return of מלכות בית דוד, and the end of the wicked kingdom) are hidden from people.

steps.title: Three things God built into the world that it needs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three features of the world that sound negative but are necessary: a body rots, the dead are forgotten, and grain rots.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three things arose in God's thought to be created, and even if they had not arisen, it would be right that they should arise: that a dead body should rot, that the dead should be forgotten from the heart, and that grain should rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. It names three things הקב"ה planned into Creation because the world could not function well without them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item looks bad at first but is really a kindness. A rotting body forces burial, so the family does not keep seeing it. Forgetting the dead lets mourners heal. Grain that rots cannot be hoarded forever, so people must sell it and others can eat. The phrase 'even if they had not arisen, it is right that they arise' stresses how logical and necessary these are.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only right that they should arise
that it will rot or decay
that he will be forgotten from the heart

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three things arose in (God's) thought to be created,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא עָלוּ — דִּין הוּא שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ:
phrases.english: and if they had not arisen, it is right that they should arise:
that a corpse should rot,
phrases.notes: So that it is buried and the family is spared.

phrases.english: and that the dead should be forgotten from the heart,
phrases.notes: So that grief eases with time.

phrases.english: and that grain should rot.
phrases.notes: So that it cannot be hoarded and must be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָלוּ בְּמַחְשָׁבָה לִיבָּרְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another numbered אגדה list on a similar theme (how הקב"ה designed the world).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rotting of the dead, forgetting of the dead, and rotting of grain were deliberately built into Creation because the world needs them.

steps.title: Another view: currency that circulates
steps.stepSummary: Some say the list includes that money should be accepted and circulate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: that currency should circulate.
steps.whatsHappening: An alternate opinion offers a different item for the list: that coins are accepted and pass from person to person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money only works if people agree to accept it. This view sees that shared acceptance as part of הקב"ה's design, because trade and daily life depend on it.

keyTerms.meaning: that it will go out, i.e., circulate and be accepted

steps.whatToRemember: These lists teach that things which seem bad (decay, forgetting) or ordinary (money working) are really part of הקב"ה's careful plan for how the world runs.

phrases.english: And some say:
that currency should circulate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate opinion on the contents of the list in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to some, the circulation and acceptance of currency is also one of the things built into Creation.

steps.title: משנה: Working on תשעה באב follows local custom
steps.stepSummary: Whether one may work on תשעה באב depends on the local מנהג, but תלמידי חכמים refrain from work everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In a place where people are used to working on תשעה באב, they work. In a place where people are used to not working, they do not work. And everywhere, תלמידי חכמים refrain from work.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Like the earlier משניות in this פרק about working on ערב פסח, it makes doing מלאכה on תשעה באב depend on local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no fixed איסור מלאכה on תשעה באב. Each place follows its own מנהג. תלמידי חכמים, however, refrain from work in every place as an extra expression of mourning for the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: a place where they had the custom
the Ninth of Av, the fast day mourning the Temple's destruction

steps.confusionAlert: Even where the local custom permits work, the משנה says תלמידי חכמים still refrain. So 'follow the local custom' does not apply equally to everyone.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב — עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: In a place where they were accustomed to work on the Ninth of Av, one works;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה — אֵין עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: in a place where they were accustomed not to work, one does not work;
and in every place Torah scholars are idle (from work).

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה to halacha with a new משנה, continuing the פרק's theme of מנהג for doing work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work on תשעה באב follows local custom, while תלמידי חכמים refrain from work in every place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the משנה's source for the halacha that refraining from מלאכה on תשעה באב is a matter of מנהג, not a full איסור.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Anyone may act like a תלמיד חכם
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a person should always conduct himself like a תלמיד חכם and refrain from work on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person should always make himself like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds to the משנה. In his view, the special practice of תלמידי חכמים (not working) is open to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא limited the extra stringency to real תלמידי חכמים. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets any person refrain from work, even where the custom is to work, without worrying that it looks like showing off. The גמרא will soon analyze the exact point of his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: a person should make himself (conduct himself as)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says only תלמידי חכמים refrain from work everywhere on תשעה באב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says every person may behave like a תלמיד חכם and refrain too.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: A person should always make himself a Torah scholar.
phrases.notes: That is, he may refrain from work on תשעה באב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting or expanding opinion on the תנא קמא's statement about תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person may conduct himself as a תלמיד חכם and refrain from work on תשעה באב.

steps.title: שמואל: In בבל, only תשעה באב is a full public fast
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the only full תענית ציבור in בבל is תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: There is no public fast in בבל except תשעה באב alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from שמואל. In בבל, only תשעה באב gets all the strict rules of a public fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasts called for rain apply mainly in ארץ ישראל, so in בבל they do not carry the full strict rules. שמואל is comparing תשעה באב to the full public fasts. The next step will ask how far that comparison goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that comes after the משנה
A public fast declared for the whole community

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
There is no public fast in Babylonia
except the Ninth of Av alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה about תשעה באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל, תשעה באב is the only fast that gets all the strict rules of a תענית ציבור.

steps.title: Does this mean twilight is forbidden? שמואל said it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads שמואל's comparison as forbidding בין השמשות on תשעה באב. Then it points out that שמואל himself said twilight is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that שמואל holds that the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden? But שמואל said: The twilight of תשעה באב is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's comparison means that twilight at the start of תשעה באב is already forbidden. It then quotes another statement of שמואל that says twilight is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשעה באב is like a full public fast, and a public fast forbids eating during בין השמשות, then תשעה באב should forbid it too. But שמואל explicitly said that the בין השמשות of תשעה באב is permitted. So his two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a possible inference)
Twilight, the doubtful time between day and night
But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: Is that to say that Shmuel holds

phrases.aramaic: תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ אָסוּר?
phrases.english: that the twilight of the Ninth of Av is forbidden?
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: The twilight of the Ninth of Av is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 7 and challenges it with another statement of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שמואל's comparison makes the twilight of תשעה באב forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself ruled that the בין השמשות of תשעה באב is permitted, which contradicts that idea.

steps.title: Suggested answer: שמואל permits twilight on every public fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל permits twilight on all public fasts, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that שמואל holds: On every public fast, the twilight is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out: maybe שמואל permits eating during twilight on every public fast. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no public fast forbids בין השמשות, then comparing תשעה באב to a public fast does not make its twilight forbidden. Both statements of שמואל could then be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you will say that Shmuel holds:
On every public fast
its twilight is permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the contradiction in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening the rule so the two statements agree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Public fasts forbid eating during twilight, so תשעה באב would too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps no public fast forbids twilight in שמואל's view.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: 'They eat while it is still day'
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says one may eat before a fast only 'while it is still day.' That seems to rule out twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: 'They eat and drink while it is still day.' What does this come to exclude? Is it not to exclude twilight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested answer with a משנה about public fasts. The משנה allows eating only 'while it is still day,' which seems to mean that eating during twilight is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'while it is still day' seem to exclude something. The natural reading is that they exclude בין השמשות. If so, public fasts do forbid twilight, and the suggested answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
What does it come to exclude?

phrases.english: But we learned in a mishna:
'They eat and drink while it is still day.'
What does it come to exclude?
Is it not to exclude twilight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that every public fast permits twilight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's phrase 'while it is still day' seems to exclude twilight from the time when eating is allowed.

steps.title: No, the משנה only excludes full nightfall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only excludes the time after dark, so twilight may still be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it comes to exclude after it has become dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not exclude twilight. It only excludes the time after full darkness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'While it is still day' can include בין השמשות. On this reading, the משנה only forbids eating once it is definitely night. That keeps the suggestion standing, so שמואל's two statements no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it has become dark

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude after it has become dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the challenge of step 10 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה excludes only full night, so public fasts may permit twilight.

steps.title: Proof attempt: 'Its doubt is permitted' must mean twilight
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the doubt of תשעה באב is permitted. The גמרא suggests this refers to twilight, which would support שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that this supports him: The only difference between תשעה באב and יום הכיפורים is that this one's doubt is forbidden, and that one's doubt is permitted. What is 'its doubt is permitted'? Is it not twilight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove שמואל right from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says that on תשעה באב, a doubtful time is permitted, and the גמרא suggests this means twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכיפורים comes from the Torah, so even a doubtful time is forbidden. תשעה באב is a rabbinic fast, so a doubtful time is permitted. Twilight is the classic doubtful time, so this would support שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it supports him
Its doubt, a case of uncertainty
Yom Kippur, a fast from the Torah

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: There is no difference between the Ninth of Av and Yom Kippur
except that this one's doubt is forbidden,
and that one's doubt is permitted.
What is 'its doubt is permitted'?
Is it not twilight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that שמואל has been defended, the גמרא tries to bring active support for him.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the twilight of תשעה באב is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting the doubt of תשעה באב with the doubt of יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Rejected: 'Doubt' means doubt about the new month
steps.stepSummary: The doubt in the ברייתא is about which day the month began, not about twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, as רב שישא son of רב אידי said: it refers to the setting of the month. Here too, it refers to the setting of the month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'Doubt' in the ברייתא means doubt about which day the new month started, not twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When it was unclear which day was ראש חודש, people outside ארץ ישראל kept holidays for two days. For יום הכיפורים the ברייתא says the doubt is forbidden, but for תשעה באב, a rabbinic fast, there is no need to fast a second day. So the ברייתא says nothing about twilight.

keyTerms.meaning: The setting of the month (deciding which day is ראש חודש)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Doubt' here does not mean the doubtful time of evening. It means the doubt about which day of the calendar is really תשעה באב.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: No, as Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
It refers to the setting of the month;
here too, it refers to the setting of the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. שמואל's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Its doubt' can mean doubt about the calendar date, not twilight.

steps.title: רבא: Pregnant and nursing women fast fully, and twilight is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that pregnant and nursing women fast the whole day on תשעה באב, as on יום הכיפורים, and that its twilight is forbidden. The same is reported in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: Pregnant and nursing women fast and complete the fast on it, just as they fast and complete it on יום הכיפורים, and its twilight is forbidden. And they said so in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a strict ruling: pregnant and nursing women must fast the full day of תשעה באב, and eating during its twilight is forbidden. This view is also reported in רבי יוחנן's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the minor fasts, pregnant and nursing women do not fast. רבא treats תשעה באב more like יום הכיפורים. He also forbids בין השמשות, which is the opposite of שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They fast and complete the fast

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a different opinion from שמואל about twilight on תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rava taught:
Pregnant women and nursing women
fast and complete the fast on it,
in the way that they fast and complete it on Yom Kippur,
and its twilight is forbidden.
And so they said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a view that disagrees with שמואל on twilight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pregnant and nursing women fast fully on תשעה באב, and its twilight is forbidden.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? He said תשעה באב is not like a public fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the report about רבי יוחנן. Another statement of his says תשעה באב is not like a public fast, apparently regarding twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: תשעה באב is not like a public fast. Is this not regarding twilight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן really forbids twilight. Elsewhere he said תשעה באב is not like a public fast, which seems to mean its twilight is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If public fasts forbid twilight and תשעה באב is 'not like' them, then twilight would be permitted on תשעה באב. That contradicts the report in step 14.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The Ninth of Av is not like a public fast.
Is it not regarding twilight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution to רבי יוחנן in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן forbids twilight on תשעה באב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן said תשעה באב is not like a public fast, which seems to mean it is more lenient regarding twilight.

steps.title: No, רבי יוחנן meant work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement is about work (מלאכה), not twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, regarding work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's 'not like a public fast' is about doing work, not about twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On תשעה באב, work is not fully forbidden; it depends on local מנהג, as stated in the משנה. That is how it differs from a public fast. On this reading רבי יוחנן can still hold that twilight is forbidden. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the twilight of תשעה באב is permitted. רבא, also in the name of רבי יוחנן: twilight is forbidden, and pregnant and nursing women fast fully. The 'work' reading of רבי יוחנן's statement is only a first attempt. The next step rejects it, and steps 18 to 22 give the readings that stand.

phrases.english: No, regarding work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the subject of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not like a public fast' refers to twilight.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to work, so רבי יוחנן can still forbid twilight.

steps.title: Work on תשעה באב Is Already Known to Depend on Custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects step 16's answer. A משנה already teaches that work on תשעה באב follows local custom. Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not forbid it, so רבי יוחנן would have no reason to state it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Work? We already learned that: "In a place where people were used to doing work on תשעה באב, they do it. Where they were used to not doing work, they do not." And even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only said that a person who sits and does not work does not look arrogant. He never actually forbade work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 16. That answer said רבי יוחנן's statement was about work. But a משנה already tells us work on תשעה באב is only a matter of custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן only meant that work is not forbidden on תשעה באב, he would be repeating an explicit משנה. Someone might think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds work is truly forbidden. The גמרא explains that he only allowed a person to refrain without seeming arrogant. He never made it an outright prohibition, so the "work" reading adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people have the custom

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view is not that work is forbidden. He only says a person may hold back from work without it looking like he is claiming to be a תלמיד חכם.

phrases.english: Work? We already learned:
phrases.notes: A surprised question that rejects the previous answer.

phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed to do work
on Tisha B'Av, they do it,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: and in a place where they were accustomed not to, they do not.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in this chapter.

phrases.english: And even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר אֶלָּא דְּכִי יָתֵיב וְלָא עָבֵיד,
phrases.english: only said that when one sits and does not work,
it does not look like arrogance,
phrases.notes: People may simply think he has no work to do.

phrases.english: but forbidding it, he did not forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 16 because it would make רבי יוחנן's statement redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יוחנן's statement "not like a תענית ציבור" refers to work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already teaches that work on תשעה באב depends on custom, and no opinion forbids it outright. So the statement would teach nothing new.

steps.title: New Reading: It Refers to the Closing Prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that "not like a תענית ציבור" means תשעה באב has no תפילת נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "it is not like a תענית ציבור" mean? It is about תפילת נעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of רבי יוחנן's words. The difference is the extra closing prayer, not twilight and not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תענית ציבור has a fourth prayer, נעילה, but תשעה באב does not. This reading keeps רבי יוחנן's statement meaningful. It also avoids any clash with the report that he holds twilight is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The closing prayer added at the end of a fast day
A public fast (for example, one declared for rain)

phrases.english: Rather: what does "it is not like a public fast" mean?
It refers to the closing prayer (Ne'ilah).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected work reading with a new interpretation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement was about work (step 16), or about twilight (step 15).
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement is about תפילת נעילה, which תשעה באב lacks.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן Wants People Praying All Day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the נעילה reading. רבי יוחנן himself said he wishes a person would pray all day long.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: "If only a person would keep praying the entire day!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading from step 18 using another statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן likes extra prayer so much that he wishes people would pray all day. So how could he say that תשעה באב has no נעילה? Surely he would welcome an extra prayer.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
If only a person would keep on praying
the entire day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the נעילה reading of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן says תשעה באב has no נעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן encourages unlimited extra prayer, so he would not exclude a fourth prayer on תשעה באב.

steps.title: Required There, Optional Here
steps.stepSummary: On a תענית ציבור, נעילה is an obligation. On תשעה באב it is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is an obligation. Here, it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating a required prayer from a voluntary one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's wish to pray all day is about voluntary prayer. On a תענית ציבור, נעילה is required. On תשעה באב a person may add it if he wishes but is not obligated. That is the difference meant by "not like a תענית ציבור".
steps.whatToRemember: On a תענית ציבור, נעילה is a חובה. On תשעה באב it is only רשות, so the two statements of רבי יוחנן fit together.

phrases.english: There (on a public fast) it is an obligation,
here (on Tisha B'Av) it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 19 and saves the נעילה reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's love of extra prayer means תשעה באב should also have נעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Voluntary extra prayer is fine, but only on a תענית ציבור is נעילה required.

steps.title: Another Reading: The Twenty-Four Blessings
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, "not like a תענית ציבור" means תשעה באב does not have the twenty-four ברכות of a תענית ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: what does "it is not like a תענית ציבור" mean? It refers to the twenty-four ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible meaning of רבי יוחנן's statement. It also has nothing to do with twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a תענית ציבור, six ברכות are added to the regular eighteen of שמונה עשרה, making twenty-four. On תשעה באב only the regular eighteen are said. This is another real difference that does not touch the twilight question.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
Twenty-four (ברכות said on a תענית ציבור)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What does "it is not like a public fast" mean?
It refers to the twenty-four (blessings).
phrases.notes: Six extra ברכות added to the eighteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reinterpretation of the statement's subject
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about the twenty-four ברכות, which are not said on תשעה באב.

steps.title: רב פפא: תשעה באב Is Like the Strictest Fasts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads "not like a תענית ציבור" as a stringency. תשעה באב is not like the first, lenient fasts but like the last, strict ones, so its twilight is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: what does "it is not like a תענית ציבור" mean? It is not like the first fasts but like the last fasts, and so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third explanation. He turns the phrase into a stringency, which fully matches the report that רבי יוחנן forbids twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasts declared for rain come in stages. The first ones are lenient and do not begin at twilight. The last ones are the strictest. רב פפא says תשעה באב is unlike the lenient first fasts and like the strict last ones, so eating at twilight is forbidden. This removes the contradiction entirely: the phrase actually supports the twilight prohibition.
steps.confusionAlert: For רב פפא, "not like a תענית ציבור" does not mean "more lenient". It means "stricter than the early public fasts".
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading lines רבי יוחנן up with רבא (step 14): the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: All three answers (נעילה, twenty-four ברכות, רב פפא) explain רבי יוחנן's statement so that it no longer contradicts the ruling that the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What does "it is not like a public fast" mean?
It is not like the first (fasts),
but like the last ones, and it (twilight) is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַאי אֵינוֹ כְּתַעֲנִית צִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, independent answer to step 15, reading the phrase as a stringency rather than a leniency.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversal: the phrase is read as a stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Not like a תענית ציבור" means תשעה באב is more lenient, so its twilight would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: תשעה באב is like the strictest public fasts, so its twilight is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say the twilight of תשעה באב is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא using a ברייתא that says the 'doubt' of תשעה באב is permitted. Its 'doubt' seems to mean its בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The only difference between תשעה באב and יום הכיפורים is that one's doubt is forbidden and the other's doubt is permitted. What does 'its doubt is permitted' mean? Doesn't it mean its twilight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב פפא, who just said that the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that on יום הכיפורים a 'doubtful' time is forbidden, but on תשעה באב a 'doubtful' time is permitted. The most natural doubtful time is בין השמשות, the twilight period when we are unsure whether it is still day or already night. If that is the meaning, the ברייתא directly contradicts רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Its doubt, a case of uncertainty
Twilight, the doubtful time between day and night

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין בֵּין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
phrases.english: They challenged: There is no difference between the Ninth of Av and Yom Kippur
except that for this one (Yom Kippur), its doubt is forbidden
and for that one (the Ninth of Av), its doubt is permitted
phrases.notes: יום הכיפורים is a Torah law, so we are strict in a doubt. תשעה באב is rabbinic, so we are lenient.

phrases.english: What does 'its doubt is permitted' mean?
Does it not mean its twilight?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין בֵּין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's claim from step 22 that the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that the בין השמשות of תשעה באב is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the doubt of תשעה באב is permitted. The obvious doubt is twilight, so twilight should be permitted.

steps.title: The 'doubt' is about which day the month began
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי explains that the 'doubt' in the ברייתא is about fixing the new month, not twilight. In every other way the two fasts are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: No. The doubt is about fixing the month. But in all other matters, both fasts are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving the word 'doubt' a different meaning, so the ברייתא no longer contradicts רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long ago, people far from ירושלים did not always know which day ראש חודש had been declared. That made the date of a holiday doubtful. For יום הכיפורים, a Torah fast, the doubtful day is in principle forbidden. For תשעה באב, a rabbinic fast, there is no need to fast the doubtful second day. The ברייתא also implies that in every other way the fasts are equal, so the twilight of תשעה באב is forbidden, just like on יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixing of the month, i.e., setting the day of ראש חודש
But by implication, it follows that

steps.confusionAlert: 'Doubt' here is NOT about what time of day it is. It is about which calendar day is really the 9th of Av.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
No, it refers to the fixing of the month
phrases.notes: There is no need to keep a second day of תשעה באב out of doubt.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְכׇל דְּבָרִים — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין.
phrases.english: But by implication, in all other matters, this and that are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: לָא, לִקְבִיעָא דְיַרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by reinterpreting 'its doubt'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Its doubt' means the twilight of תשעה באב, which would make twilight permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Its doubt' means doubt about the date of ראש חודש. Otherwise the two fasts are equal, so twilight is forbidden on both.
steps.whyThisMatters: The implied line 'in all other matters they are equal' becomes the basis for the next step, which supports רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: This supports רבי אלעזר: no finger in water on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The implication that תשעה באב equals יום הכיפורים in all other matters supports רבי אלעזר. He forbids dipping even a finger in water on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, who said: A person may not put his finger into water on תשעה באב, just as he may not put his finger into water on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא, as just explained, backs up a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשעה באב and יום הכיפורים are equal in every matter except the date-doubt, then the washing rules must match too. On יום הכיפורים even a finger may not be dipped in water. So the same is true on תשעה באב, exactly as רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports (a proof for someone's view)

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
It is forbidden for a person to stretch out his finger
into water on the Ninth of Av,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָסוּר לְהוֹשִׁיט אֶצְבָּעוֹ בְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: just as it is forbidden to stretch out his finger on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the implication from step 24 ('in all other matters they are equal') as a proof for a different אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that even dipping a finger in water is forbidden on תשעה באב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא as explained by רב שישא: תשעה באב equals יום הכיפורים in everything except the date-doubt

steps.title: A ברייתא compares תשעה באב to a תענית ציבור, where partial washing is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says תשעה באב differs from a תענית ציבור only regarding work. On a תענית ציבור only washing the whole body is forbidden. So partial washing should be allowed on תשעה באב, against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The only difference between תשעה באב and a תענית ציבור is that on one, work is forbidden, and on the other, work is permitted where that is the custom. This implies that in everything else they are the same. Yet about a תענית ציבור it was taught: when they said washing is forbidden, they meant only the whole body, but not the face, hands, and feet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to attack רבי אלעזר's strict ruling about putting a finger in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא makes תשעה באב equal to a תענית ציבור in every way except work. A separate ברייתא says a תענית ציבור only forbids washing the whole body, while washing face, hands, and feet is fine. Put the two together, and on תשעה באב dipping a finger should also be allowed, which contradicts רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A communal fast, declared for a crisis such as drought
In a place where the custom is (to do it)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says work is forbidden on the תענית ציבור and permitted on תשעה באב (where that is the custom). It is not the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין בֵּין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְתַעֲנִית צִיבּוּר
phrases.english: They challenged: There is no difference between the Ninth of Av and a communal fast
except that on this one (the communal fast), doing work is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה מוּתָּר בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ.
phrases.english: and on that one (the Ninth of Av), doing work is permitted in a place where people are accustomed to it.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶם — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין.
phrases.english: This implies that in all their other matters, this and that are equal.
Yet regarding a communal fast, it was taught:
When they said 'washing is forbidden,'
they said it only about one's whole body,
but about his face, his hands, and his feet, they did not!
phrases.notes: So on תשעה באב, partial washing (like a finger) should be allowed, against רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין בֵּין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְתַעֲנִית צִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר, whose view was just supported in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that even a finger may not be dipped in water on תשעה באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תשעה באב equals a תענית ציבור in everything except work. A תענית ציבור only forbids washing the whole body. So on תשעה באב washing face, hands, and feet, and certainly dipping a finger, should be permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא starts to respond to the challenge against רבי אלעזר. His actual answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב פפא is about to answer the challenge, and his words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears here, so the content of the answer is not yet known. It will need to explain how the ruling on washing in a תענית ציבור fits with רבי אלעזר's strict rule for תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the answer to the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not yet stated; continues on the next amud
